title: No June has no ar no oysters. But there are people like things high. Tainted game.
html_source:
Since the 18th century, oysterfishing was prohibited in France, the United Kingdom and the United States during the months without the letter “r” in their names (i.e. May, June, July and August). These close seasons were instituted to combat the decline in oyster populations due to constant overfishing.

As Ulysses is set in June and “June has no ar”, Bloom concludes that there are currently no oysters being served.

The next two sentences (starting with “But there are…”), however, show Bloom sharing the widely held belief that the “r-rule” was originally implemented because of a lack of reliable refrigeration. After noting “no ar no oysters”, he is thus led into thinking about spoiled goods (“things high”, “tainted game”), continuing his train of thought.

It is worth noting that connoisseurs are adhering to the “r-rule” up until today, even though both the refigerating and breeding problems have been solved for a long time.

For further information about the “r-rule”, click here (in German).
